name: PassRole viability fails CLOSED on a non-canonical SUBJECT partition (S2-passrole-allstmts, SUBJECT axis)
note: Same CLASS of fail-open as the ARN-spelling axis, reached through the OTHER side of the exact-equality partition compare: the SUBJECT partition (ctx.partition). The role-ARN partition/account tokens are validated against KNOWN_PARTITIONS / 12-digit, but the subject partition was trusted VERBATIM (only .trim()). A non-canonical spelling of the subject's OWN partition ('AWS', 'Aws', '*', 'aws-gov', 'AWS-US-GOV') therefore made a viable same-account, same-real-partition critical PassRole->service path read as cross-partition and get CONFIDENTLY demoted critical->medium (PARTITION_MISMATCH), so analyze() rated the path MEDIUM while scan() - which sanitizes the partition against KNOWN_PARTITIONS - kept it CRITICAL/exit 1: analyze() MORE permissive than scan() for byte-identical input (browser==CLI parity violation), and the sole medium finding slips under a high-threshold gate as CLEAN. FIX (in the shared engine, the single source of truth): validate ctx.partition with the SAME KNOWN_PARTITIONS rigor as role-ARN partitions; an unrecognized/non-canonical subject partition token is treated as NOT confidently known and NEVER drives a confident cross-partition demotion. viableSameAccount: a viable aws same-account path stays CRITICAL under every non-canonical partition (no demotion needed - the account reasoning defaults to 'aws' and the path is genuinely viable), matching scan() exit 1. crossPartitionSameAccount: an aws-us-gov same-account role under a non-canonical subject partition fails CLOSED as UNKNOWN viability (severity kept at critical, requiredUnknowns:['subjectPartition'], scan exit 3) rather than a confident PARTITION_MISMATCH medium; the canonical control (subject partition really 'aws-us-gov') is viable/critical/exit 1, proving no over-correction.
